description.narrative:
The expected outcomes of the Activity will be: a) Knowledge-sharing and promoting the use of evidence to decision-makers, academics and practitioners. b) Stronger partnerships between the global community of academics and practitioners working to improve the cost-effectiveness of humanitarian and development activities. c) A clear roadmap for mainstreaming cost-effectiveness analysis in UN programming and impact evaluation. d) New inter-agency partnerships and commitments for joint impact evaluation evidence generation across the humanitarian-development sectors. e) A shared understanding and renewed momentum among Member States and donors to support a more unified and evidence-driven UN system.
The planned main areas of the Activity are: - Global Impact Evaluation Forums in 2025 and 2026 - Inclusive Regional Impact Evaluation Prioritisation Workshops - Multi-Agency Partnerships · Evidence prioritisation and meta-analyses · Inclusive co-design of multi-agency impact evaluation portfolio frameworks for demand-led, multi-agency evaluations. · Collaboration protocols. · Technical assistance from WFP to partners interested in joint evaluations. · Coordination support for UNEG working group and other collaborative initiatives. · Joint fundraising for multi-agency impact evaluation portfolio frameworks - Impact Evaluation Capacity-Building · Development of training modules on impact evaluation and cost-effectiveness analysis. · Training for relevant stakeholders
